title: What If You Lit a Flame on the Space Station?

scenes.text: What if you lit a flame in space? It would turn into a ball.
On Earth, hot gas rises and pulls in fresh air, which stretches a flame upward.
Without gravity, hot gases do not rise. They move outward, so the flame forms a sphere.
On the space station, NASA saw spherical blue flames speckled with tiny yellow dots of glowing soot.
Oxygen reaches the flame slowly, so it burns cooler, and often goes out.
Even stranger: fuel can keep burning as cool flames, too faint for the naked eye to see.

description:
What if you lit a flame in space?
Without gravity, it forms a blue ball, burns cooler, and can keep burning as invisible cool flames.
